That is a capital letter, it just looks like that.
Go and quickly rewrite everything all over again.
Are you kidding me, this is already the third letter!
If you want to be a chef, learn to write documents!
Did you think of who to introduce your father to today?
I have two options right now.
Look, you two are together at work too.
Hello, Dad, should I pour for you as usual?
I was walking nearby and decided to visit my son.
Alright, I will not bother you two.
I will go sit quietly at a table alone.

examples.text: Врач сказал, что всё в порядке.
examples.trans: The doctor said that everything is fine.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Напротив, я решил лично поблагодарить вас.
examples.trans: On the contrary, I decided to thank you personally.

examples.text: Вообще-то я ещё ничего не решил.
examples.trans: Actually, I have not decided anything yet.

examples.text: Как это ты ещё не решил?
examples.trans: What do you mean you have not decided yet?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ведать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to visit / check on'.

examples.text: Гулял рядом и решил проведать сына.
examples.trans: I was walking nearby and decided to visit my son.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и проведать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to visit on time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'son' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я как к родному сыну относился.
examples.trans: I treated him like my own son.

examples.text: Гулял рядом и решил проведать сына.
examples.trans: I was walking nearby and decided to visit my son.

examples.text: Сынок, а почему ты рано пришёл?
examples.trans: Son, why did you come home so early?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Спокойной тебе ночи и сладких снов.
examples.trans: Good night to you and sweet dreams.

examples.text: Ладно, тогда уже завтра всё расскажем.
examples.trans: Alright, then we will tell everything tomorrow.

examples.text: Ладно, я не буду вам мешать.
examples.trans: Alright, I will not bother you two.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сейчас всё выглядит очень некрасиво.
examples.trans: Right now everything looks very bad.

examples.text: Нам пора наконец перестать так прятаться.
examples.trans: It is time for us to finally stop hiding like this.

examples.text: А вы не пойдёте с нами?
examples.trans: Are you not coming with us?

meanings.en: to be in the way, to hinder
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to disturb', paired with 'помешать'.

examples.text: Я бы сказал, языковой барьер помешает.
examples.trans: I would say a language barrier will get in the way.

examples.text: Языковой барьер им помешает.
examples.trans: A language barrier will get in their way.

examples.text: Ладно, я не буду вам мешать.
examples.trans: Alright, I will not bother you two.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: А вы не пойдёте с нами?
examples.trans: Are you not coming with us?

examples.text: Ну, в принципе, можно и пойти.
examples.trans: Well, in principle, we can go.

examples.text: Пойдём, мы вас на улице подождём.
examples.trans: Let us go, we will wait for you outside.

посидеть.gloss: to sit for a while; to stay (with someone)

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сидеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sit for a while; to stay (with someone)', paired with 'сидеть'.

examples.text: Вот я и подумал спокойно посидеть.
examples.trans: So I thought we could sit calmly together.

examples.text: Посиди с Викой.
examples.trans: Stay with Vika for a while.

examples.text: Давай посидим в кафе.
examples.trans: Let's sit in a café for a bit.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Тихо, милая, давай сейчас посмотрю глаз.
examples.trans: Easy, darling, let me look at your eye right now.

examples.text: Пойду посижу тихо за столиком один.
examples.trans: I will go sit quietly at a table alone.

examples.text: Тише, дети спят!
examples.trans: Quiet, the children are asleep!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Я только за такое хорошее решение.
examples.trans: I am all for such a good decision.

examples.text: Ладно, тогда уже завтра всё расскажем.
examples.trans: Alright, then we will tell everything tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'table' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пойду посижу тихо за столиком один.
examples.trans: I will go sit quietly at a table alone.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.

examples.text: Хотите сесть за свободный столик?
examples.trans: Would you like to sit at an available table?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я запускаю один новый интересный проект.
examples.trans: I am launching an interesting new project.

examples.text: Пиши заявление и уходи с кухни!
examples.trans: Write your resignation letter and leave the kitchen!

examples.text: Тебе не кажется, что отцу одиноко?
examples.trans: Does it not seem to you that your father is lonely?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Работать главным шеф-поваром, я не знаю.
examples.trans: To work as head chef, I do not know.

examples.text: А он позвал меня работать шефом.
examples.trans: And he invited me to work as a head chef.

examples.text: Вообще-то я его немного сам доработал.
examples.trans: Actually, I improved it a little myself.
